questionText: What is idempotency in REST APIs and why does it matter?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can define HTTP idempotency, explain why a lost response makes it useful, and separate intended effects from response equality.

claims.statement: An idempotent HTTP method has the same intended effect after several identical requests as after one request.
Safe methods, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent by standard semantics, and idempotency allows automatic retry after a communication failure under the RFC conditions.

examples.title: Repeated DELETE with different responses and the same final effect

validation.expected: Both requests leave the target association absent

visuals.title: Retry after the first response is lost

notes: Idempotency-Key is described as an application API contract, not as an RFC 9110 method guarantee.
